title: Human design vs. machine learning for AI
reading: The slide contrasts hand-coding rules with learning from data for building AI systems. On the left it poses the challenge of "coding" the rules — asking whether one could actually enumerate the rules for recognizing a cat — and states the underlying idea that humans are often good at making decisions but poor at explaining them. On the right a diagram illustrates the two routes by which a cat-recognizing robot can be built.

visuals.description: Center-right: a cat photo with the label "cat" cycles via yellow circular arrows to a robot icon. A blue arrow labeled "Design" points down into the robot from above; a blue arrow labeled "Learn" points up into the robot from a dashed box below containing three labeled cat photos and the text "Data collection".
visuals.assertion: A cat recognizer can be obtained either top-down by human design (coding rules) or bottom-up by learning from a collection of labeled cat images.

concepts.name: Rule-based (hand-coded) AI
concepts.why_it_matters: Requires humans to articulate explicit rules, which is hard for perceptual tasks.

concepts.name: Machine learning from labeled data
concepts.why_it_matters: Sidesteps the need to state rules by learning them from collected examples.

concepts.name: Tacit knowledge (deciding vs. explaining)
concepts.why_it_matters: Motivates why learning replaces manual rule specification.

verbatim_spans: "Coding" the rules: Can you list the rules of recognizing a cat?
Humans sometimes are good at "making decisions" BUT are not good at "explaining decisions"
